items.question: How do Indian manufacturers find distributors in the UAE?
items.answer: Approach distributors and importers directly about portfolio fit, then shortlist on coverage. For an Indian formulation company, outreach to owners and business development heads at UAE distributors led to 12 partner meetings and 3 distributors shortlisted. Follow-ups covered customer segments, existing product lines and support for market entry, so only real fits reached a meeting.

items.question: Do you work with companies based in the UAE, or only exporters?
items.answer: Both. Two of our four UAE campaigns were for companies selling into the UAE, and two were for firms working there: a brokerage that booked 20 meetings with employers before their benefits renewal, and an IT provider that booked 16 meetings with multi-office firms. For UAE-based lead generation by city, see our Dubai and Abu Dhabi pages.

items.question: Is cold email allowed in the UAE?
items.answer: B2B outreach to business decision-makers is common in the UAE, but data protection rules apply. The UAE has a federal Personal Data Protection Law, and free zones such as DIFC and ADGM have their own. We contact business roles only, say who is writing and why, and stop at the first opt-out. Confirm specifics with counsel.

items.question: How long before the first UAE meetings?
items.answer: Campaigns usually go live about 18 days after onboarding, and first qualified conversations typically come in weeks 3 to 4. Distributor searches take longer to close, because each partner is qualified on coverage and after-sales capability before a shortlist. Timing is not guaranteed and depends on your product and market.
